name: Punk
context: The sisters were in it from the very beginning, from glam to punk

name: Manic Panic
heard: manic panic / manika / many panicked / panic music
context: The first punk boutique in America, opened on St. Marks Place on 7 July 1977 - later the semi-permanent hair-dye brand the sisters built up without investors from $250 each

name: Tish & Snooky
heard: scythian / snoky / snook / stooky / strookie / tish / titian
context: Guests: the Bellomo sisters from the Bronx - backing singers in the first Blondie, the Sic F*cks, and since 1977 Manic Panic, the shop on St. Marks Place that became the hair-dye brand

name: The Sic F*cks
heard: 16th broadcast / sick bucks / sick fox / sick fuck / sick, folks / sick. fox / six bucks / six flux / six fucks
context: The sisters' own band, in nuns' habits; at first they kept the name from their mother

name: Manic Panic store, St. Marks Place
heard: the shop / the store / your shop
context: The shop itself: everyone let in, the hosts rehearsing Proud Mary, a 50-cent badge as some days' takings, the first customer who needed a shopping bag

name: James St. James
context: Host; a Manic Panic regular in the club-kid years. He did the Downtown Dukes and Divas show with them

name: England
context: The sisters flew over with partner Gina from 1977, sold vintage sunglasses and biker rings and brought back hair dye not sold in the US

name: Manic Panic: Living in Color
heard: in the book / living in color / the book / your book
context: The sisters' book: their story in their own words, other people's memories, hair-colour tutorials and a list of celebrity clients; RuPaul wrote the intro

name: Cyndi Lauper
context: Shopped for vintage at the store when she was still blonde, in Blue Angel days; the sisters say her leap into hair colour helped launch her career and theirs

name: Debbie Harry
context: Saw the sisters in a revue and invited them to Blondie rehearsals; took them thrift shopping in her 69 Camaro and showed them a warehouse of unworn vintage shoes

name: Electric blue Manic Panic hair
heard: blue hair / blue like / blue was / electric blue
context: Fenton's first dye job, the colour of the sisters' trickiest early shade

name: Tomata du Plenty
context: With Gorilla Rose he got Debbie and Chris to come and see the sisters - which is how they joined Blondie

name: Cotton candy pink and pastels
context: James wanted cotton candy pink in 84 when it didn't exist - you mixed Manic Panic with conditioner; today Pastelizer does it

name: Quaaludes
context: James admits Quaalude envy - he never tried one

name: Fenton Bailey
context: Co-host; dyed his hair electric blue with Manic Panic as a student at Oxford, then had to dye it back black as an extra in Heaven's Gate

name: Randy Barbato
context: Co-host and co-founder of World of Wonder; one of the Fabulous Pop Tarts, with the sisters on backing vocals

name: Blondie
context: The sisters sang backing vocals in the early band; they say they were a little jealous when it made it without them, but got over it fast

name: Gina
context: The third partner at the start of Manic Panic; she left within the first year

name: New York
context: The sisters as free-spirited New Yorkers singing in dives in 1977 - and still singing in dives

name: New Jersey
context: Thrift runs with Debbie; the punk bashers came from Long Island or Jersey

name: The New Jersey Nightingales look
context: Big blonde number-one bouffant wigs, Nerf footballs cut in half for torpedo bras, tight dresses or polyester lounge-act jumpsuits from a thrift store
fashion: Blonde bouffant wigs, torpedo bras, polyester jumpsuits

name: Bronx
context: Where the sisters grew up and still lived with their mother when the shop opened, commuting in

name: Mary Kay
context: James: the sisters are the Mary Kays of punk

name: Club Kids
context: Every club kid came into the store and got the 20 percent rock-star discount; James calls the sisters their godmothers

name: Punk pointy stilettos, Beatle boots and sharkskin

name: Fred Rothbell-Mista
context: Promoter who put the sisters in his lounge act as his New Jersey Nightingales; ran the upstairs at the Limelight and helped with Downtown Dukes and Divas

name: Bronx Psychiatric Center
context: Where the sisters' mother worked; they say the name Manic Panic came from there

name: Snooky's super-short Mudd Club dress

name: Judy Tenuta
